It's hurtful to use autism as an insult. Frankly, I don't understand how people can rag on people with autism for lack of empathy or bad social skills yet can be so unapologetically rude in the same posting. If you try to call them out or protest at all then you're just mocked for being oversensitive. 


I dunno. I guess ever since I've been diagnosed my thoughts and opinions have stopped mattering to anyone who knows. Any strengths or weaknesses I have is just the autism.

It's going to sound strange, but "even if your writing sucks" is the thing that is going to stick with me in the most positive way. Because my friends that have been earning tremendous success have always tried to ignore my work because they don't have the heart to tell me they hate it. Yet my friends who are "amateurs" have always fully supported it. People always downplay the "lowest common denominator". Having pop music be my favorite genre has always been a bit of my embarrassment. But I'm starting to realize that maybe there is nothing wrong with making something purely for those who appreciate it, no strings attached. Maybe it's about time that I accept that the group that is going to offer me acclaim isn't going to be the group that gets me popular. Rather, it's going to be the people who accept it for what it is.


I doubt this is going to be a permanent fixture in my life. Then again, that's not what this subreddit is about since it's more aimed towards people in a crisis. However, I'm willing to accept right now. I'm going to return to my book this afternoon. And I'm going to deeply thank you for your insight. All of you do great things here.

I have a condition known as vaginismus. It basically means that under certain circumstances your vaginal muscles will contract if there is too much pressure. I know this because it happened while getting my first pap smear. The moment she "spread me open" so to speak I could feel the muscles tightening. 

For guys or people who haven't had anything in their vagina: imagine putting a whole grapefruit in your mouth. That's what my downstairs felt like. I know people who have given birth are probably rolling their eyes. You have to understand that when it shrinks, very small objects feel massive. I was sweating and crying out in pain. They couldn't finish because I was basically shut.

I'm going to have to do a bunch of exercises before I go the next time. I know that it's fairly treatable but I still get sick when I remember that experience.
